title: 3 crore voters cut? Petitioner's claim, SC notice #Shorts
description:
Maharashtra SIR voter list deletions, Supreme Court notice to Election Commission, Form 6 for deleted voters: on 26 October the Supreme Court sought the Commission's reply on a plea over the state's voter-roll revision. The petitioner's counsel says about 3 crore of Maharashtra's 9 crore voters, roughly 1 in 3, were struck off after the draft rolls were published, and that deleted voters are being asked to fill the new-voter form. These are his figures. The Commission hasn't responded yet, and the Chief Justice said in court that nobody will be prosecuted. The next hearing is on 5 November. Should deletions pause until the court decides?

Subscribe to Sawaal for the day's political news and the questions behind it.

Sources: LiveLaw, The Wire, India Legal, LawChakra, Daily Pioneer (all 26 Oct 2026).
This video is commentary. The anchors and some visuals are AI-made.
#SIR #SupremeCourt #Maharashtra #VoterList #Shorts

script:
SAWAAL, Short 6 of 6 today. English version only; Hindi dub is posted automatically on the same channel. Status: live. Category: 25 (News & Politics). Length about 52 s, 9:16.

VOICES: Aditya en-IN-PrabhatNeural (Hindi dub hi-IN-MadhurNeural, pitch +6Hz). Nisha en-IN-NeerjaNeural (Hindi dub hi-IN-SwaraNeural, pitch +4Hz). Looks per channel config.

SCRIPT (fact-checked)
ADITYA: "Struck off the voter list? You may be asked to fill the new-voter form. And the petitioner says it's three crore people in Maharashtra."
NISHA: "On 26 October, the Supreme Court issued notice to the Election Commission on a plea against Maharashtra's voter-roll revision, the SIR. The bench: CJI Surya Kant, with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana."
ADITYA: "Senior counsel Arvind Datar says about 3 crore of Maharashtra's 9 crore voters were struck off after the draft rolls came out, 1.22 crore for 'logical discrepancy'. These are his figures; the Commission hasn't responded yet. The court declined to extend the claims deadline or stop the final roll without first hearing the Commission."
NISHA: "The detail behind the headline: Datar says deleted voters are being asked to file Form 6, the form for new voters, declaring they haven't voted before. He argued that could expose them to a false-statement charge. The CJI said in court, 'Nobody will be prosecuted.'"
ADITYA: "Three questions for the 5 November hearing. What is the official deletion number? Will there be a separate form for deleted voters? Will the no-prosecution assurance be written into a court order?"
NISHA: "Opinion: a voter who was already on the roll shouldn't have to sign a new-voter declaration to get back on it. Follow Sawaal for 5 November. Should deletions pause until the court decides?"
